subject: Request: deterministic headroom window & eviction-notice SLA for Fennel Health
messages:
From: Sara Cho <sara@fennelhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@fennelhealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — deterministic headroom & eviction notice

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing requirements for our reserved-GPU plan and have one ask that will determine whether we move forward with the Dedicated contract as-is or request an addendum.

Short version: for our nightly batch scoring window (02:00–05:00 UTC) we need deterministic headroom on reserved GPUs and an advance eviction-notice SLA for in-flight requests. Specifically:
- Guarantee X1 (8) reserved GPUs available to our pool during that 3h window (no preemption except under documented maintenance).
- If preemption is required, send an eviction notice with a minimum of 30 seconds remaining on the request so our client can gracefully retry/fallback.
- Queueing behavior: requests queued at tail during the window must not be arbitrarily dropped; we need a documented retry/backoff semantics.

I've attached an appendix that outlines the traffic profile and why the 30s notice matters (we have synchronous websocket flows). Can your Dedicated team accept these terms or propose acceptable guardrails?

Attaching: Fennel_SLA_Appendix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Sara Cho
Head of Platform
Fennel Health
[sara@fennelhealth.com]

From: jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
To: Sara Cho <sara@fennelhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — deterministic headroom & eviction notice

Sara —

Thanks for the clear ask and the appendix. Appreciate the traffic profile — that helps a lot. We're generally able to support carveouts for short, well-scoped windows but need to coordinate with SRE and Sales on the exact mechanics and any associated commitments (credits, runbook, observability hooks).

Quick next steps from our side:
1) Ben (cc) to draft a commercial addendum with a proposed guarantee and conditional credits if we miss the headroom commitment.
2) Marissa (cc, SRE) to propose the technical acceptance criteria (how we signal eviction, metrics to monitor, and fallback options).
3) Lauren (cc, account lead) to align on escalation and reporting cadence.

Can we set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the appendix and sign off on the technical constraints? If you prefer, we can share a short runbook draft before the call.

—Jordan

From: ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — proposed commercial terms

Jordan / Sara —

Following up with a proposed commercial approach so we have something to discuss on the call:

Proposal highlights (commercial):
- We can reserve 8 GPUs (A100 equivalent) for Fennel's pool between 02:00–05:00 UTC daily for the initial 3-month pilot.
- Guarantee: 95% availability of that reserved capacity during the window (applies to production hours detailed in the appendix).
- Eviction notice: we can provide a controlled preemption flow where live requests receive an eviction signal via a header+event at least 30s prior to preemption, provided the request uses our runtime hooks.
- Remedies: if availability falls below guaranteed levels in a billing month, we offer pro-rated service credits up to 10% of that month's Dedicated fee (capped). Credits require evidence via our shared observability dashboard and linked request traces.

Open items for the call:
- Exact handshake for the eviction signal (webhook vs runtime header).
- Fallback model: do you want us to automatically route to a smaller quantized model during preemption windows?
- Contract term and credit caps.

We can tighten language after engineering confirms the signal guarantees.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Lauren Bishop
Account Lead, Strategic Customers
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sara Cho <sara@fennelhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — technical runbook draft

Folks —

Draft SRE acceptance criteria and runbook notes below (high level):

1) Eviction signal mechanics
- We'll emit an eviction_event via: Runtime-Status: preempting and a POST to a customer webhook (if configured).
- Signal must be consumed within 5s by customer SDKs to guarantee graceful abort/retry within 30s.

2) Deterministic headroom
- We can pin 8 GPUs to the tenant's pool during 02:00–05:00 UTC. Headroom guarantee is operationally scoped: excludes pre-scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- If autoscaler is triggered outside the pinned window, we won't evict the pinned GPUs during 02:00–05:00 unless there's a safety-critical incident.

3) Queueing behavior & retries
- Tail queue uses FIFO with backpressure; we will not drop queued requests during the window. Long-pending requests (>120s) will be surfaced to the customer dashboard as "at-risk" so you can decide to cancel or continue.

4) Observability and evidence
- We'll share per-request traces, eviction event logs, and a 95th/99th percentile latency dashboard for the window for proof of compliance.

5) Remedies & acceptance testing
- If availability <95% in a month, remedy = pro-rated credit as Ben proposed. Acceptance tests: we'll run 3-day soak test with your traffic profile and both parties must sign off before addendum activation.

Next steps: if you agree with the above, we'll produce a short runbook PDF and an SLA addendum draft for legal. We can include a DocuSign link for the addendum in the HubSpot deal.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Dedicated Services
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Cho <sara@fennelhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — confirmation

1) We will instrument the runtime hooks (our SDK team confirms consumption within 3s).
2) For fallback model routing during preemption, we'd prefer an automatic redirect to a quantized model if latency stays within bounds (we'll bring the model owner on the call).

Let's confirm the call for tomorrow 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC. Please share the runbook draft beforehand if possible. Looking forward to locking this into the addendum.

Best,
